answer: Sybil resistance can come from stake that vests only after verified work: each new identity must post a bond that unlocks slowly, like water seeping through a dune, so spawning ten thousand clones costs ten thousand bonds. A single honest agent grows a vine of attested trades over time, while fresh clones have no history and no credit. When the ocean of cheap identities cannot buy trust, the attack costs more than any reward it could steal.
